title: O002-B1 Naive Persistence Baseline Audit
purpose: Quantify how much of prospective CASE affect forecasting is captured by the simplest possible no-training baseline: predict future valence/arousal as the last pre-anchor same-axis reported state.

horizons.shift_0: original target [0,5] s; predictor prior report [-5,-1] s
horizons.shift_1: target from next 10 s anchor; predictor-end to target-start gap about 11 s

prediction_rule: For each axis and row i, yhat = prior_<axis> from row i. For shifted horizons, target = y_<axis> at row i+h within the same subject×video only.
training: None. This baseline learns no parameters and therefore cannot leak subject or stimulus identities from training.
metrics: crossed subject×video bootstrap 95% CI for mean cell MAE
interpretive_rule: This is a diagnostic benchmark, not a new primary endpoint.
If naive persistence is already close to fitted prior-model error, manuscript framing must emphasize baseline strength / incremental information rather than model novelty.
If naive persistence is materially worse, learned time/context calibration contributes beyond simple carry-forward.
Do not infer psychological mechanism from predictive persistence.
firewalls: No physiology conclusion is drawn from B1 alone.
No post-result threshold will be invented to call closeness; comparisons to G1/G2 will report absolute and relative MAE differences transparently.
